solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Finally retired, Bill has houses in the country

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it governs

parts.note: the last letter of retired
AC, short for account, a bill
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who has finally retired buys property out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the country' suggests rural England, but the houses are Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian second home or cottage out of town, so dachas are country houses.

clue.text: Beloved learner in enterprise

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: daring is boldness, enterprise
L for learner, as on the plates of British learner drivers

explanation.surface: A beloved trainee shows initiative in a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enterprise' suggests a company, but here it is the quality of boldness.
explanation.definitionFit: A darling is a much-loved person, a beloved.

clue.text: Funny male in charge undermining firm

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
M is the abbreviation for male
IC is short for in charge

explanation.surface: An amusing man in charge undermines the company.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'undermining' puts the first pieces under the firm's letters, so CO comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic as an adjective means humorous, causing laughter.

clue.text: Possibilities to convert indigenous people?

parts.note: to convert is to alter
natives are people born in a place

explanation.surface: Missionaries weigh up chances of converting local people.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternatives are options or other choices, possibilities to pick from.

clue.text: Some quiet husband is so

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the run of letters across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A quiet husband is described as being just so.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus and so are synonyms meaning therefore or in this way.

clue.text: Devon town house with no metal put up

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A house in a Devon town is built without metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England. In a down entry the reversed part reads upwards beneath the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Honiton is a market town in east Devon, famous for its lace.

clue.text: Difficult to walk when energy is limited

indicators.note: is limited means hemmed in on both sides by the other piece

parts.note: to step is to walk
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Walking is hard work when you are low on energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep can mean excessive or hard to accept, as a demanding price or a hard climb.

clue.text: Asian language restriction in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out over the air, so we go by how it is spoken

parts.note: a tie is a restriction or constraint

explanation.surface: A limit placed on an Asian language in radio programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Thai is the official language of Thailand in south-east Asia.

clue.text: Unorthodox logician, sort who may examine skulls?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the person

indicators.note: unorthodox means not in the usual form, so the letters take an unusual order

parts.note: all the letters of these words

explanation.surface: An unconventional thinker is the sort to go poking at skulls.
explanation.definitionFit: Craniology is the scientific study of skulls, so its practitioner would examine them.

clue.text: Rich team surprisingly losing one second fixture

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement, so the letters are jumbled
losing tells us a letter drops out of the mix before it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I, here removed

explanation.surface: A wealthy football team unexpectedly loses one game and must play again.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of RICH TEAM and rearrange the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch is a second game between the same opponents, a repeat fixture.

clue.text: Cooker of fruit, missing ring

indicators.note: missing signals that something is left out of the word for the fruit

parts.note: a citrus fruit
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A cooker for fruit has lost one of its rings.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the O off the front of ORANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large kitchen stove, a cooker with several ovens and hotplates.

clue.text: Sally at home with dog and boy around lunchtime?

indicators.note: around means the last part goes on either side of the time

parts.note: at home means in
a cur is a mongrel dog
a son is a boy
one o'clock, written as the numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone at home with the dog and a boy goes out around lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Lunchtime is one o'clock, so it gives the Roman one, I, which goes inside SON. The question mark flags that loose equation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden attack or sortie, as is an incursion into enemy territory.

clue.text: Sheep in place turned around

indicators.note: turned around means the word faces the other way, read from its end

parts.note: to place is to put

explanation.surface: A sheep in its pen turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tup is a ram, an uncastrated male sheep, in farming dialect.

clue.text: Obtained pigmeat for New York, informally

parts.note: obtained means got
ham is meat from a pig

explanation.surface: Someone bought some pork to take to New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Gotham is a nickname for New York City, popularised by Washington Irving and later Batman.

clue.text: This pet suffering? Worst possible thing

indicators.note: suffering suggests being knocked about, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: all the letters of these words

explanation.surface: An owner looks at a sick pet and thinks it the worst thing ever.
explanation.definitionFit: The pits is an informal idiom for the very worst, the lowest point imaginable.

clue.text: Ten numbers recalled in poem

indicators.note: recalled, as in called back, sends the letters back the way they came

parts.note: taken as written
NOS is the abbreviation for numbers

explanation.surface: Ten numbers remembered and put into a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a fourteen-line poem with a fixed rhyme scheme.

clue.text: Stay due to be organised for 24 hours

indicators.note: to be organised means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: all the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A visit is planned to last a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuesday is one day of the week, an example of a 24-hour period.

clue.text: Line that is found in story

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
i.e., Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: One line in a story is said to hold the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: A story can mean a falsehood, as when a child is told not to tell stories.

clue.text: Turning up, make merry in bar

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: to revel is to make merry

explanation.surface: Someone arrives to have a good time in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it is a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever is a rigid bar used to pry or lift things.

clue.text: I'd recount changes in institute

indicators.note: changes says the letters before it are altered into a new order

parts.note: all the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone plans to recount the changes made at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'institute' looks like a noun, a college, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute a scheme is to set it up, to introduce or bring it in.

clue.text: Friar unable to move, needing head released

indicators.note: head released means the first letter is let go

parts.note: stuck means unable to move

explanation.surface: A friar is trapped and needs his head freed.
explanation.walkthrough: Friar Tuck is the jolly friar in the Robin Hood legends.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar Tuck is the monk of Robin Hood's band, so the friar names him.

clue.text: Brown river sweeping away hotel

indicators.note: sweeping away means clearing something out, so a letter goes

parts.note: the Humber is an estuary in north-east England
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A brown river in flood carries off a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is an earthy brown pigment and the colour named after it.

clue.text: Spokesperson's wickedness, admitting nothing

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: vice is wickedness
nothing is zero, O

explanation.surface: A spokesperson's corruption is said to amount to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice can be a person who speaks for a group, as in the voice of the workers.

clue.text: Cheated, in two different sleeping places!

parts.note: the first place to sleep, a baby's cot
the second place to sleep

explanation.surface: Someone was unfaithful, sleeping in two different beds.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words for places to sleep, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To crib is to copy dishonestly, as in an exam, so cribbed means cheated.

clue.text: Flower was a climber?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: went up, the past tense of a verb of ascent

explanation.walkthrough: 'was a climber' reads like a description of a climbing plant, which the bloom can be; but it is also simply the past tense of going up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a familiar garden bloom and the past tense meaning ascended or went up.

clue.text: Sparkling son has to wait

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to tarry is to linger or wait

explanation.surface: A bright-eyed son has to wait his turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Starry describes something shining or glittering like the stars in the sky.
